summary: Describes how to carry XML-RPC messages, in which a client asks a server to run a procedure and return a result, over BEEP instead of HTTP. It defines the mapping onto a BEEP profile. It is an experimental specification.

plainLanguage.summary: XML-RPC lets a client ask a server to run a procedure and return a result. RFC 3529 maps those messages onto BEEP channels carried over TCP.

questions: how does xml-rpc work without http
what port does xml-rpc over beep use
what is the xmlrpc.beeps url scheme
subtitle: A BEEP profile for sending XML-RPC requests and responses over TCP.

tldr.problem: XML-RPC defines messages for remote procedure calls, and this memo specifies how to carry those messages over BEEP instead of relying on HTTP.
tldr.mechanism: A BEEP channel identifies the XML-RPC profile and resource. The client sends a request in a BEEP MSG, and the server returns its response in a BEEP RPY.
tldr.outcome: RFC 3529 is Experimental and is updated by RFC 8553. It defines the xmlrpc.beep and xmlrpc.beeps URL schemes and registers TCP port 602.

today: RFC 3529 is an Experimental memo and is updated by RFC 8553. It specifies XML-RPC messages carried by BEEP over TCP.

sections.title: XML-RPC Messages over BEEP
sections.content:
XML-RPC encodes a procedure call and its parameters, or the result of a call, as XML. RFC 3529 specifies a BEEP profile for transferring those messages between a client and a server.

The profile does not change what an XML-RPC request or response means. It changes the transport: BEEP carries the XML-RPC messages over TCP.
sections.plainLanguage: The request still names the procedure and its inputs, and the response still carries the result. BEEP provides the connection that carries those messages.

sections.title: Starting the Profile and Selecting a Resource
sections.content:
The profile is identified by http://iana.org/beep/transient/xmlrpc when a BEEP channel is created. The initiating peer first sends a bootmsg with a required resource attribute. The server sends bootrpy if it recognizes the resource; otherwise, it sends an error and the profile remains in its boot state.

Once the profile is ready, the initiator can send XML-RPC calls. The resource identifies the service path for the channel, and the BEEP serverName identifies the server's virtual host.
sections.plainLanguage: The client first names the service resource it wants. The server confirms that resource before the client sends procedure calls.

sections.title: Request and Response Messages
sections.content:
XML-RPC requests and responses use UTF-8 with the media type application/xml. A client sends each request in a BEEP MSG; the server returns the corresponding response in RPY.

The profile does not use a BEEP ERR for an XML-RPC fault in a one-to-one exchange. The server places the XML-RPC response, including a fault response, in RPY.
sections.plainLanguage: A client sends one call in a message, and the server returns one response message. A failed call still uses the normal response form.

sections.title: URL Schemes and Privacy Tuning
sections.content:
The memo defines two URL schemes: xmlrpc.beep and xmlrpc.beeps. The URL path becomes the BEEP resource; if the path is absent, the resource defaults to /. A domain name without a port is resolved using the xmlrpc-beep TCP service name and DNS SRV procedures.

The xmlrpc.beeps scheme requires the BEEP session to be tuned for privacy before the XML-RPC profile starts. When TLS is used, the client must verify that the server certificate matches the URL authority. The RFC registers TCP port 602 for XML-RPC over BEEP.
sections.plainLanguage: The URL identifies the server and resource. The scheme ending in s requires privacy tuning, and TLS use requires checking the server's identity.
